builds.name: Reference: Ranked jungle core
builds.goal: Reference for Shyvana: the core and runes ranked Emerald+ jungle players use most (12,532 ranked Emerald+ games with this core on OP.GG, patch 16.20, 57.8% win rate).
builds.hypothesis: A transforming melee fighter who earns defenses through takedowns and uses empowered dragon spells to extend close combat. The current jungle provider core anchors this plan; later slots are observed options or reviewed kit completions. Core in purchase order: Trinity Force → Spear of Shojin → Death's Dance. Press the Attack keystone as played in those games. Remaining slots: Plated Steelcaps, Sterak's Gage, Randuin's Omen.
builds.summary: The proven jungle baseline: Trinity Force → Spear of Shojin → Death's Dance, with Press the Attack.
testPlan: Play it in jungle as your control build. Follow the purchase order; the core (Trinity Force → Spear of Shojin → Death's Dance) is what ranked players complete first.
Record kills, deaths, damage dealt and the minute you finish each core item, then compare other builds against these numbers in similar games.
Adapt the last two items to the enemy team: armor or magic resist against fed carries, anti-heal against healing, penetration once enemies stack resists.
failureConditions: Your results with this build fall clearly below the 57.8% ranked baseline over several games in the same role.
The enemy team composition makes the core items poor answers; swap the flexible slots before abandoning the core.
tradeoffs: Proven and predictable, so opponents know what to expect. It is a starting point, not the best build for every matchup.
The observed core and individual options do not establish six-item build statistics. Late slots are kit-based inferences.
Six-slot completion is our kit-based inference, not an observed six-item win-rate build.  Situational options replace an appropriate slot; they are not added as a seventh item.
buyOrder: Core in purchase order: Trinity Force → Spear of Shojin → Death's Dance.
Boots after the first item unless the lane needs them earlier.
coverageNotes: Source: OP.GG ranked Emerald+ solo/duo, patch 16.20, checked 2026-10-14. Core items and rune page are observed; later slots are observed options or reviewed completions. Win rates describe those games, not a prediction for yours.
builds.author: Rift Build Lab ranked data

Active: Shyvana's next Attack strikes the target and the surrounding area dealing [10 / 15 / 20 / 25 / 30 + (1.1) × AD + (0.3) × AP] physical damage. This Ability may be Recast after an Attack or short delay within the next [4] seconds.

Dragon Form: Shyvana gains an additional Recast, causing her to bite the target of her next Attack dealing [(10 / 15 / 20 / 25 / 30 + (1.1) × AD + (0.3) × AP) × (1.5)] true damage.

Shyvana launches a fireball at the target location dealing [50 / 65 / 80 / 95 / 110 + (0.6 / 0.65 / 0.7 / 0.75 / 0.8) × AP] + [0.05] Max health magic damage and Slowing by [0.3] for [2] seconds. It explodes upon striking an enemy or reaching its terminus.

Upon striking a champion, large monster, or reaching its terminus it triggers a pulse of fire that deals [(50 / 65 / 80 / 95 / 110 + (0.6 / 0.65 / 0.7 / 0.75 / 0.8) × AP) × (1.25)]  + [(0.05) × (1.25)] Max Health magic damage and Slows by [(0.3) × (1)] for [2] seconds. The fireball leaves behind a trail for [2] seconds that deals [characterLevelBreakpoints(start=15, perLevel=0, changes=[{"mLevel": 11, "mAdditionalBonusAtThisLevel": 5.0, "__type": "Breakpoint"}, {"mLevel": 16, "mAdditionalBonusAtThisLevel": 5.0, "__type": "Breakpoint"}]) + (0.05) × AP] magic damage per second.

Shyvana wraps herself in flames for [2.5] seconds, gaining [60 / 80 / 100 / 120 / 140 + (0.12) × Stat(12)[statFormula=2]] Shield, increased by [(60 / 80 / 100 / 120 / 140 + (0.12) × Stat(12)[statFormula=2]) × (0.3)] per nearby enemy champion and [0.25] Move Speed, increased to [(0.25) × (1.75)] when moving towards enemy champions.

When the effect ends, the Shield is broken, or upon Recast the area around her detonates, dealing [80 / 100 / 120 / 140 / 160 + (0.65) × AP] magic damage.

builds.name: Dragon third bite
builds.summary: Use the inspected reworked dragon Q's extra recast as a mixed-damage finish.
builds.goal: Use the inspected reworked dragon Q's extra recast as a mixed-damage finish.
builds.hypothesis: Q attacks reduce its cooldown and carry a health-based magic on-hit. The active can recast, and dragon form adds a third bite with a 1.5 multiplier and true damage. Nashor, Dusk and Terminus test real attack delivery while R's finite Fury constrains form duration.
testPlan: Required state: Dragon form with recorded Fury and passive stacks; all three Q attacks connect.
Separate first, second and dragon-only third Q packets, then test Dusk repeat without assuming active duplication.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Form expires before the bite or kiting prevents cooldown-reducing attacks.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Legacy twin-bite or burnout interactions do not describe this Emberstrike/Inferno Aegis kit.
Confidence: speculative. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Nashor's Tooth, Dusk and Dawn, Terminus, Riftmaker, Rabadon's Deathcap, Berserker's Greaves. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Situational adaptation: Magic matchup
builds.goal: Situational adaptation for Shyvana: adapt to the specified fight rather than assume one universal build
builds.hypothesis: A transforming melee fighter who earns defenses through takedowns and uses empowered dragon spells to extend close combat. Use the current reworked dragon/human abilities and finite Fury. Q attacks lower Q cooldown and have current HP/AD effects; do not import an old E-only AP build without measuring it. MR and nearby magic amplification test durable contact against magic pressure.
builds.summary: MR and nearby magic amplification test durable contact against magic pressure.
testPlan: Kit question for Shyvana: Use the current reworked dragon/human abilities and finite Fury. Q attacks lower Q cooldown and have current HP/AD effects; do not import an old E-only AP build without measuring it.

Start with the early core (Hollow Radiance or other MR first when justified) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Compare against the reference route at the same level, gold spent, finite stacks and opponent setup. Record unused gold; isolate an item change before changing runes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Resource: Fury. Do not treat mana regeneration as Fury recovery; Nimbus replaces Manaflow when that Sorcery row is used.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: MR and nearby magic amplification test durable contact against magic pressure. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern. Choose the opponent profile this defensive route is intended to address, then repeat against the wrong damage type.

Q evidence: Shyvana's next attack strikes both the target and the surrounding area. This Ability can be recast. While in Dragon Form, it gains an additional recast, dealing massive damage to a single target. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: MR is wasted against the wrong threat; nearby aura range and healing eligibility matter.

The route fails Shyvana's stated kit question: Use the current reworked dragon/human abilities and finite Fury. Q attacks lower Q cooldown and have current HP/AD effects; do not import an old E-only AP build without measuring it.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility.
tradeoffs: MR is wasted against the wrong threat; nearby aura range and healing eligibility matter.
Full cost 15,600 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
Counter-items are conditional. Change boots/defense for the real matchup, then record the modified setup.
buyOrder: Hollow Radiance or other MR first when justified. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Keep appropriate boots while building the early core; swap boots only when the measured matchup justifies it.
Abyssal Mask, Spirit Visage, Jak'Sho, The Protean are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Resource: Fury. Do not treat mana regeneration as Fury recovery; Nimbus replaces Manaflow when that Sorcery row is used.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.
Source formulas remain in Champion kit. Symbolic values, unresolved tokens and helper records are evidence to inspect, not a certified executable simulator.
Legal source item/rune references were checked; retained map flags cannot prove every live-shop condition. Confirm shop eligibility, exact on-hit/on-attack rules and real proc cooldowns in game.

builds.name: Aegis crowd recovery
builds.summary: Convert nearby champions into a larger shield and a timed dragon detonation heal.
builds.goal: Convert nearby champions into a larger shield and a timed dragon detonation heal.
builds.hypothesis: W shield includes a bonus-health Stat term and increases per nearby champion; dragon W heals on champion detonation using missing health. Visage supports both shield and heal, Riftmaker converts health to AP and Abyssal boosts nearby magic damage from W/E. R adds finite bonus health.
testPlan: Required state: Dragon form, nearby champion count and missing health recorded before W recast.
Measure shield and heal with one versus three nearby champions at matched missing health, then compare human form.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.

The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Human W does not inherit the dragon-only detonation heal.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
